sourceType: Official Rajasthan Tourism website (Government of Rajasthan)
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Founded 1553 by Maharana Udai Singh II as new capital of Mewar Kingdom, in the fertile circular Girwa Valley southwest of Nagda (first Mewar capital). Called 'Venice of the East' / 'City of Lakes'. Known for zinc and marble.

places.name: Pratap Memorial (Moti Magri)
places.location: Moti Magri hill, overlooking Fateh Sagar
places.facts: Bronze statue of Maharana Pratap on his horse Chetak; Chetak died carrying Pratap to safety after the Battle of Haldighati.

places.name: City Palace
places.facts: Conglomeration of courtyards, pavilions, terraces; main entrance via triple-arched Tripolia gate with 8 marble porticos (Maharanas historically weighed in gold here for charity); Surajgokhada (Balcony of the Sun); Mor Chowk (peacock glass mosaics); Chini Chitrashala (blue/white ceramics); nightly sound and light show at Manak Chowk.

places.name: Lake Palace
places.location: Island in Lake Pichola, near Jagmandir
places.facts: Originally Jagniwas, built 1743-1746 as a summer palace; now a hotel; black and white marble walls with semi-precious stone inlay; faces east.

places.name: Jag Mandir
places.facts: Also 'Lake Garden Palace'; construction began 1620, completed ~1652; royal summer resort; sheltered Prince Khurram (later Shah Jahan) during his rebellion against Jahangir; said to have inspired the Taj Mahal.

places.name: Monsoon Palace (Sajjangarh)
places.facts: 19th-century palace/hunting lodge built by Maharana Sajjan Singh; originally intended as an astronomical center, plan cancelled at his premature death; panoramic city views.

places.name: Ahar Museum
places.location: Near the Ahar cenotaphs of the Maharanas of Mewar
places.facts: Small collection of earthen pottery, sculptures, archaeological finds some dating to 1700 BC; 10th-century metal Buddha figure.

places.name: Jagdish Temple
places.facts: Built 1651 by Maharana Jagat Singh I; Indo-Aryan architecture; dedicated to Vishnu; three-storied, carved pillars, painted walls.

places.name: Fateh Sagar Lake
places.facts: Artificial lake connected to Pichola by canal; houses Nehru Island and the Udaipur Solar Observatory (only observatory in India on a lake island, modeled on Big Bear Lake, California); inaugurated by Duke of Connaught, originally 'Connaught Bundh'.

places.name: Lake Pichola
places.facts: Named after the village Picholi; houses Jagniwas (Lake Palace) and Jagmandir islands; City Palace on eastern bank; sunset boat rides popular.

places.name: Saheliyon Ki Bari
places.facts: Built by Maharana Sangram Singh II as a garden for women (Garden of the Maidens); marble elephants, fountains, kiosks, lotus pool, small museum.

places.name: Bird Park, Gulab Bagh
places.facts: 5.11-hectare bird park, 12 enclosures; parrots, macaws, cockatoos, Great White Pelican, Green Munia; 28 total bird species.

places.name: Sukhadia Circle
places.facts: Small pond with a 21-foot, three-tiered carved marble fountain; illuminated at night; surrounded by gardens.

places.name: Bharatiya Lok Kala Mandal
places.facts: Cultural institution for folk art/culture/songs/festivals of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh; includes a museum of Rajasthani artefacts.

places.name: Bagore Ki Haveli
places.facts: Built 18th century by Amar Chand Badwa, Prime Minister of Mewar; 100+ rooms; costumes and modern art displays; classical haveli glass/mirror work; evening cultural dance shows.

places.name: Shilpgram
places.location: 7 km west of Udaipur, near Fateh Sagar
places.facts: Rural Arts and Crafts Complex, 70 acres, surrounded by Aravallis; living museum of folk/tribal lifestyles of the west zone; hosts the 10-day Shilpgram Festival, 21-30 December.

places.name: Udai Sagar Lake
places.facts: Construction started 1559 by Maharana Udai Singh; dam on the Berach river; ~4km long, 2.5km wide, ~9m deep at its deepest.

places.name: Doodh Talai Lake
places.location: On the road to Pichola Lake, Udaipur
places.facts: Nestled between hillocks; includes Deen Dayal Upadhyay Park and Manikya Lal Verma Garden.

places.name: Jaisamand Lake
places.facts: Second largest man-made sweet-water lake in Asia; built to hold back the Ruparel River; large central island home to various bird species; popular weekend picnic spot.

places.name: Navalakha Mahal, Gulab Bagh
places.facts: 19th-century structure; Maharishi Dayanand stayed here for ~6.5 months from 10 Aug 1882 at the invitation of Maharana Sajjan Singh; completed writing Satyarth Prakash here.

places.name: Wax Museum (Hollywood Wax Museum)
places.facts: Interactive wax-figure museum; also offers 9D cinema, gaming zone, mirror maze, horror show.

places.name: Udaipur Fish Aquarium (Under the Sun)
places.facts: India's first hi-tech virtual fish aquarium claim; 156+ varieties of sea/freshwater fish from 16 countries at launch (up to 1500 planned); 125m gallery; touch pool for children; largest fish (Arapaima) up to 9 feet.

places.name: Vintage Car Collection
places.facts: Vintage/classic cars (Cadillac, Chevrolet, Morris etc.) owned and used by the Maharanas of Udaipur.

places.name: The Crystal Gallery
places.facts: One of the largest, most complete collections of F. & C. Osler cut glass in existence; most commissioned by Maharana Sajjan Singh from 1878, larger furniture pieces from 1881; includes a jewel-studded crystal carpet and a crystal royal punkah (fan) with Mewar sun emblem; Osler founded Birmingham 1807.

places.name: Nagda / Sahastra Bahu Temple (Sas-Bahu Temples)
places.facts: Ancient site at Aravalli foothills, traces to 6th century AD; Sahastrabahu ('one with a thousand arms', a form of Vishnu) temple complex, 9th-10th century AD, ASI-listed heritage monument; elaborate Ramayana-themed carvings; adjoining Jain temple of Adbhutji.

places.name: Badi Lake (Jiyan Sagar)
places.facts: Artificial lake built by Maharana Raj Singh, named Jiyan Sagar after his mother Jana Devi; built to counter drought effects, proved valuable during the 1973 drought; surrounded by three chhatris.

places.name: Sajjangarh Biological Park
places.location: Foothills of Bansdara hills, outside Sajjangarh Wildlife Sanctuary
places.facts: 36-hectare park; carnivores and herbivores in near-natural habitat enclosures; visitable on foot or paid golf-cart.

places.name: Menar
places.location: ~48 km from Udaipur on Udaipur-Chittorgarh road
places.facts: Village known for migratory bird sightings in winter at two ponds, Brahm Talab and Dand Talab; a favoured spot for birders.

howToReach.rail: Udaipur City railway station; Mewar Express and other trains from Delhi/Mumbai
howToReach.air: Maharana Pratap Airport (Dabok), ~22 km from city
howToReach.road: NH-48 via Ajmer from Delhi; well connected to Jaipur, Ahmedabad
